title: Passenger registration
text: The system shall register a passenger using name, email, phone and password, normalize email, and reject duplicate email or invalid fields without creating an account.
acceptance: POST /api/auth/register returns 201 for valid data, 409 for duplicate email, and 400 for invalid data; no password or hash is returned.

title: Authentication and session lifecycle
text: The system shall authenticate valid credentials, issue an opaque bearer session, reject invalid credentials, expire sessions after 24 hours, and invalidate the current session on logout.
acceptance: Valid login returns 200 and token; wrong credentials return generic 401; five failures trigger a 300-second lock (429); expired or logged-out tokens fail protected requests.

title: Train search
text: The system shall search active trains by source, destination and date, requiring source to precede destination in the stored stop sequence.
acceptance: GET search uses date=YYYY-MM-DD, returns 200 with matching trains or an empty list; invalid criteria return 400; class, fare, time and sort filters obey documented inputs.

title: Train details
text: The system shall display train number/name, requested route, departure, arrival, duration and fare, with ordered schedule and class fares available for inspection.
acceptance: Search summary, schedule and fares endpoints agree with fixture values; unknown train returns 404.

title: Seat availability
text: The system shall return class-wise current available seats for a train and date.
acceptance: For each class, availableSeats equals totalSeats minus sum of seat_reservations.seats for the same train/date/class; reservations on another date do not reduce it.

title: Passenger booking form
text: The system shall let an authenticated passenger select a train, date and class, enter one to six passengers and obtain a fare/availability preview before confirmation.
acceptance: Valid preview returns 200 with passengerCount, farePerPassenger, totalFare and availableSeats, and writes no booking; unauthenticated preview returns 401.

title: Passenger validation
text: The system shall validate all passenger fields before preview and confirmation.
acceptance: Name is 2–60 permitted characters; age is an integer 1–120; gender is M/F/O; zero or more than six passengers is rejected; indexed errors identify the failing passenger and no partial booking is written.

title: Final availability check
text: The system shall recheck active train, class and available capacity inside the confirmation transaction.
acceptance: If seats were consumed after preview, confirmation returns 409 and creates no booking, passenger, inventory or success audit rows.

title: Unique PNR
text: The system shall create a unique ten-digit nonsequential PNR for every successfully confirmed reservation.
acceptance: Two successful bookings have distinct ten-digit PNR strings persisted under a UNIQUE database constraint; PNR lookup retrieves the owner ticket.

title: Atomic seat reservation
text: The system shall allocate one distinct seat per passenger and reduce available inventory by exactly the passenger count on successful confirmation.
acceptance: For n passengers, exactly n seats and one linked quantity-n reservation are committed; availability drops by n once, and failed confirmation leaves it unchanged.

title: Ticket confirmation
text: The system shall display confirmed booking reference, train, travel date, class, passengers, seat numbers and fare.
acceptance: POST booking returns 201; authenticated GET /api/bookings/{pnr} returns 200 with the same ticket; unknown or another owner PNR returns 404.

title: Booking history
text: The system shall display the authenticated passenger’s confirmed and cancelled bookings in newest-first order.
acceptance: GET /api/bookings returns only the current user’s records including ticket details; a new account has an empty list.

title: Eligible cancellation
text: The system shall permit the owner to cancel a confirmed booking when the configured cutoff is satisfied, and reject duplicate or late cancellation.
acceptance: Default cutoff is 24 hours before the first stored departure interpreted in UTC including first-stop day offset; below cutoff or already cancelled returns 409; successful cancellation returns 200 and CANCELLED.

title: Refund quotation and recording
text: The system shall display the eligible refund before confirmation and persist the calculated refund on successful cancellation.
acceptance: Read-only quote shows eligibility and policy; default refund is floor(totalFare × 90 / 100) integer rupees; configured 0–100 percent is honored; this is a record, not fund settlement.

title: Seat restoration
text: The system shall restore only the cancelled booking’s seats exactly once within the cancellation transaction.
acceptance: Linked reservation is removed; availability increases by passengerCount; second cancellation does not increase it; released seats can be reused without active duplicates; failure rolls back refund/status/inventory/audit.

title: Booking ownership
text: The system shall prevent a passenger from viewing, quoting or cancelling another passenger’s booking, irrespective of supplied owner fields.
acceptance: Other-owner requests return 404; missing/invalid/revoked bearer sessions return 401; cancellation service checks the authenticated owner inside its transaction.

title: Administrative train management
text: The system shall allow active administrator sessions to create, update and deactivate train, ordered stop and class/fare/capacity data.
acceptance: Passenger access is 403 and unauthenticated access 401; valid changes appear in search/details; deactivation hides new bookings while old tickets/cancellation remain accessible; invalid/failed changes roll back.

title: Booking audit events
text: The system shall persist timestamped booking-created and booking-cancelled events with actor, booking, train and PNR identifiers.
acceptance: One matching event is committed with each successful transition; failed transactions leave no success event; authorized admin can retrieve events.

title: Response time
text: Search and normal booking shall provide a user-visible response within 3 seconds for at least 90% of requests under normal project load.
acceptance: Measure search and booking separately; each p90 ≤3 seconds. Local runner: 20 search and 20 booking requests at four clients; browser rendering is separately inspected and the local result is not production capacity certification.

title: Concurrent integrity
text: The system shall prevent allocation of one train/date/class seat to two concurrent confirmed bookings.
acceptance: Simultaneous reservation tests show no duplicate active seat and no overselling; direct duplicate inserts are rejected by the seat trigger.

title: Safe errors
text: The system shall return clear validation and safe error messages without database internals, stack traces or credentials.
acceptance: Invalid JSON, wrong types, oversized bodies/IDs and simulated database failures return controlled errors with no SQL/stack/secret disclosure.

title: Availability and recovery
text: The system shall support normal project use and recover gracefully from temporary application/database failures while retaining consistent committed data.
acceptance: Restart after clean stop and abrupt process termination preserves committed tickets/inventory/audit; SQLite integrity check is ok; rollback tests retain consistent data. Unrecoverable media corruption is outside this acceptance test.

title: Password protection
text: The system shall persist passwords only as salted secure one-way hashes.
acceptance: Stored PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 values differ for identical passwords; production default 600000 iterations; no plaintext password is persisted or returned.

title: Role enforcement
text: The system shall restrict all administrator functions to currently authorized administrator sessions.
acceptance: Passenger/anonymous/revoked sessions are rejected; role is reloaded from database on every authenticated request; public registration cannot choose ADMIN.

title: Responsive user interface
text: The system shall provide a readable, usable core booking flow on common desktop and mobile viewports.
acceptance: At 390×844 and 1366×900, controls/text remain reachable and no horizontal page overflow prevents use; browser evidence must identify each flow actually exercised on each viewport.

title: Auditability
text: The system shall maintain persistent auditable timestamped records of successful booking and cancellation actions.
acceptance: Events can be correlated to ticket/actor and retrieved through admin audit; preserved after restart; failed actions have no success event.

title: One-way password storage
text: The system shall never store plaintext passwords and shall use salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with bounded iteration parsing and constant-time derived-hash comparison.
acceptance: Hash inspection and verification tests pass; identical passwords have distinct salts; malformed or implausible stored iteration counts fail safely; weaker hashes upgrade after successful login.

title: Authentication and authorization
text: The system shall enforce authentication, current role and booking ownership for every protected operation.
acceptance: Anonymous/invalid sessions fail with 401; passenger admin attempts fail with 403; foreign bookings are hidden with 404; session hashes only are persisted and logout revokes access.

title: Secure communication
text: The system shall support HTTPS/TLS for credential and reservation exchange in a supported deployment and validate it over a live connection.
acceptance: Real executable with certificate/key completes trusted local TLS handshake and authenticated HTTPS workflow; incomplete TLS configuration fails startup. Plain HTTP development mode is not evidence of compliance for a hosted deployment.

title: Input safety
text: The system shall validate untrusted input, use parameterized SQL and safely render user-derived content to reduce injection risks.
acceptance: SQL/script/control-character/wrong-type/oversized inputs cannot alter schema or execute unintended scripts; invalid data produces controlled errors and no unintended writes.

title: Secret-safe diagnostics
text: The system shall exclude passwords and bearer authentication values from logs, URLs and error messages.
acceptance: Access logs include method/path/status while dropping query values; secret redaction tests and error/URL inspections show no submitted password or raw token.
